answer_markdown:
4. OD-1, OD-2 and Python conversion coverage

OD-1 is a repaired operator package, with no option or recommendation selected (D3:1648-1667). It now preserves the distinctions required by R-OD1: body-only (o) repairs some release execution but leaves checked Q.Value Posts; (i-a) needs real GNATprove model binding, independently verified full arithmetic, and migration of direct Ada users; (i-b) is a concrete result-type/API migration; (ii) is a rebuilt-runtime identity change with layout, Length/index/base arithmetic, automatic vector, multiplication/division, controlled-copy and checked-cost obligations; (iii) retires an original executable capability and is explicitly ineligible; (iii') adds a successor while closing nothing about the originals. Approval of a runtime/API choice is not acceptance.

The installed runtime substantiates the breadth of (ii): RT/s-shabig.ads:46-71 contains the bounded Length subtype, Digit_Vector and fixed Len/Neg record representation; RT/s-genbig.adb:135 and :580 declare automatic operand-sized vectors and a sum-of-lengths bound; :1176-1194 contains Bignum_Limit and the retained Storage_Error branch. Merely editing Normalize would not discharge those other limits or costs. No cap-removal success or loaded-runtime claim is made here. V3-RC3 must correct the checked-cost material that OD-1 references.

OD-2 keeps E0 OPEN; supplies interpreter-wide E1 and scoped-codec E2 as operator packages; and explicitly rejects a finite higher limit, per-call toggling, catch-and-refuse and a new size-admission “repair” (D3:1689-1699,1802-1809). E1 now distinguishes launcher/service, pre-import direct-module entry, -I/-S trusted child startup, inherited runpy, examiner restoration, re-executed candidate payload, protected-custody, original campaigns, scripts and the extension's inherited interpreter (D3:1704-1716). Its evidence must observe configuration before each first relevant conversion (D3:1726-1731). This is a configuration proposal, not observation of the actual WORLDLINE interpreters. The direct BUILD-TOOL interpreter native/build_guard.py is inventoried but has no explicit class/disposition in the E1 table; add a startup disposition or an independently reviewed lexical/magnitude bound before declaring that package complete (Appendix A:27,217-219; C5/native/build_guard.py:33-51).

The original minimum-limit defect is repaired. This review's own /usr/bin/python3 reports Python 3.14.7, default_max_str_digits=4300, str_digits_check_threshold=640 and current limit=4300; these are interpreter observations, not workload-process facts. The primary [Python integer-conversion documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.14/builtins/stdtypes.html#integer-string-conversion-length-limitation) says the minimum enabled limit is 640, zero disables it, and signs do not count as digits. E2's scanner-validated decimal chunks of at most 640 digits and final formatted chunks of at most 640 digits therefore satisfy every admitted conversion limit, including 640 (D3:1739-1748,1755-1756). This addresses the conversion guard only; arithmetic allocation and superlinear time remain O-PY-COST.

Fresh JACKAL MCP responses were status=exact, with these verbatim parsed inputs/results: parsed=4300+1, exact=4301 (K-43); parsed=4000-640, exact=3360 (K-44); parsed=6*640+461-4301, exact=0 (K-45). The displayed chunk partition is consistent. These are exact rational computations outside the Lean certificate chain, not a parser/serializer or universal correspondence proof. Complete response non_claims are retained in checks.json.

The passive AST reproduction matches all of Appendix A's listed direct-call sites and scope partitions: 192 observed direct json calls; no unmatched listed sites or syntax errors. It never imports WORLDLINE. It also found a missed semantic JSON site: import json as _json at scripts/decisive_evaluation_test.py:260, then _json.dumps at :264-275. Its keywords include indent=2. A direct-name-only scan cannot support “Complete site list” or exclude this site by spelling. Include the alias, classify its actual report operands, and scan aliases/forwarded JSON callables before finalizing the inventory. JACKAL returned status=exact, parsed=192+1, exact=193 for the direct list plus that known omitted call; this is a minimum demonstrated census, not a proof of exhaustive data flow.

Appendix A:10-11 also falsely says none of the listed Python files differs from C4. C5/runtime/worldline/proof_manifest.py appends candidate pin material at :1024-1029 after C4's ending at :1023. The json.loads site at :921 is unchanged, but file byte identity is not. Record the actual pin-only delta and exact source identities rather than claiming byte equality. The audit and hashes are retained in checks.json.

E2-b has a material semantic defect. Its “sort_keys by code point” (D3:1761) conflicts with the package's explicit integer-key support (:1755). Installed /usr/lib/python3.14/json/encoder.py:357-377 sorts original key objects before converting integer keys to text. For integer keys 2 and 10, original numeric sorting and sorting their decimal strings differ; mixed incomparable key types can raise TypeError before conversion. A replacement must preserve that ordering/failure behavior, as well as all settings, hooks, escaping, numeric subclasses, floating/NaN handling, circular references and recursion behavior. E2-a's private _intstr hook is a viable direction conditional on the pinned-CPython/C-encoder correspondence evidence (:1758-1759); it is not selected.

The exclusion criterion also needs precision: “integers … below 10**640” (Appendix A:44; D3:1770,1782) must mean an absolute-magnitude bound for integer formatting, plus a lexical digit-count bound for non-JSON decimal parsing. A one-sided signed inequality or small parsed value alone does not bound input conversion length. Preserve canonical strict UTF-8, -0 re-encoding, duplicate-key hooks and every original refusal independently of that audit (D3:1737-1748,1762-1765; Appendix A:251-272).

Appendix A.3 correctly labels non-JSON data-flow classification OPEN and lists categories its AST scan did not enumerate, rather than treating absence of a direct call as evidence of safety (Appendix A:274-298; D3:1779-1785). PR request IDs and outside-runtime/protected sites are now in scope. Required change V3-RC1 completes the package corrections above, synchronizes decisions.json and any displayed totals, and adds codec controls for integer-key ordering and mixed-key failures. No OD-1 or OD-2 choice is made.
